content:
Users can now create fully licensed music, voiceovers, and sound effects using the Adobe Firefly AI assistant. Here is the full introduction.

Firefly audio tools officially available

Adobe previously partnered with the Berklee College of Music to conduct a survey examining the workflows and challenges of video creators, musicians, and marketers. Adobe said all respondents reported using music in their videos, with 32.7% using AI-generated music. 43.2% of respondents identified legal and copyright risks as the biggest barrier to using music, while 38.9% blamed licensing fees.

Adobe today announced that the Generate Music tool is officially available on Firefly, along with the launch of two other tools: Generate Speech and Generate Sound Effects.

Generate Music can create original, fully licensed tracks based on video length and mood, allowing users to use the music on any platform without worrying about licensing or takedown issues. Generate Speech converts text into clear, natural-sounding voiceovers, with users able to choose between Adobe's own Firefly voice model or ElevenLabs' option. Generate Sound Effects creates custom sound effects based on on-screen actions, timing, and rhythm.

The company emphasized that music generated by Generate Music is fully licensed and can be used directly in finished products; like Generate Speech and Generate Sound Effects, no additional subscription is required to generate commercially usable assets.

Generate Music can analyze video content and automatically build editable prompts based on the style it deems most appropriate. Users can also adjust parameters such as tempo, energy, and length before pressing the "Generate" button to receive four options.

Through Generate Speech, users can add emotional expressions and pronunciation markings to specific parts of their scripts; while Generate Sound Effects allows users to input text prompts or record audio as references to generate sound effects.

Below is content provided by Adobe:

The new tools are now available on the Adobe Firefly desktop and mobile web applications.

Adobe expands AI model lineup within Firefly

Additionally, Adobe today also announced the arrival of Gemini Omni Flash on Firefly, allowing users to "combine video, audio, and image inputs with text to provide more ways for video development and iteration..."

This move comes days after the company added Runway Aleph 2.0 and Kling 2.0 to its third-party model toolkit, which already included models from Google, Kling AI, Luma AI, OpenAI, Runway, and Adobe itself.
